issue.title: [snappi] tgen_port_info skips get_snappi_ports_for_rdma on single-DUT/single-ASIC, so parameterized iterations reuse the same Tx/Rx ports

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

High

### Description of the bug

_tgen_port_info_ in [tests/common/snappi_tests/snappi_fixtures.py](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-mgmt/blob/master/tests/common/snappi_tests/snappi_fixtures.py) is the common fixture that selects Tx and Rx ports for Snappi RDMA tests.

On each call it:

1. Reads multidut_port_info from tests/snappi_tests/variables.override.yml (rdma_ports: named Tx/Rx sets per testbed subtype).
2. Reads Snappi/DUT port mapping from the testbed *links.csv via get_snappi_ports.
3. Decides how to combine those two sources.

Pytest parametrizes the fixture through generate_skeleton_port_info() in tests/conftest.py. When an override exists, each list entry is a separate iteration, for example long-to-short-400Gbps vs short-to-short-400Gbps. Those entries exist so the same test can run on different Tx/Rx pairs.

The override path currently looks like this (current master):
```
snappi_ports = get_snappi_ports
if is_snappi_multidut(duthosts):
    snappi_ports = get_snappi_ports_for_rdma(
        get_snappi_ports,
        rdma_ports,
        tx_port_count,
        rx_port_count,
        testbed
    )
testbed_config, port_config_list, snappi_ports = snappi_dut_base_config(
    duthosts, snappi_ports, snappi_api, setup=True)
```

_is_snappi_multidut()_ is True for modular chassis / multi-DUT setups and False for a typical single-DUT, including single-ASIC.

When it is False:

- get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() is not called.
- rdma_ports from variables.override.yml is ignored after the length checks.
- The full get_snappi_ports list from *links.csv is passed straight into snappi_dut_base_config().
- get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() is what maps each override subtype onto a distinct Tx/Rx subset (match peer_port / peer_device against rdma_ports, then sample tx_port_count / rx_port_count). Skipping it means every parametrized iteration uses the same port set.

That wastes runtime and hides topology-specific coverage the override was written for (short-to-long vs long-to-short, different speeds, and so on).

Critical - This is more relevant when single-asic had following classification of ports.
- Uplink vs Downlink ports.
- Different speed combinations on DUT (interfaces) like 100, 400 and 800Gbps.

In this case, we want to run tests based on variables.override.yml file so that all type are selected, based of off variables.override.yml file.

The same is_snappi_multidut gate exists in setup_ports_and_dut() in tests/snappi_tests/files/helper.py and should be treated as the same class of bug.

When multidut_port_info / rdma_ports is not present, parse_override() returns is_override=False and tgen_port_info already uses snappi_port_selection (<speed>-<category> from *links.csv). That path must stay a single valid combination per capability (for a single-ASIC DUT, typically only single_linecard_single_asic). It must not invent extra iterations that reuse the same ports.

### Steps to Reproduce

Steps to reproduce

1. Use a single-DUT / single-ASIC Snappi testbed (is_snappi_multidut(duthosts) is False; num_asic == 1).
2. Add at least two multidut_port_info subtypes for that testbed in tests/snappi_tests/variables.override.yml, with different Tx/Rx ports. Example pattern:

```
<testbed-name>:
  multidut_port_info:
    - long-to-short-400Gbps:
        rx_ports:
          - hostname: <dut>
            port_name: Ethernet0
        tx_ports:
          - hostname: <dut>
            port_name: Ethernet128
    - short-to-short-100Gbps:
        rx_ports:
          - hostname: <dut>
            port_name: Ethernet144
        tx_ports:
          - hostname: <dut>
            port_name: Ethernet80
```

3. Confirm those ports exist in the matching ansible/files/*links.csv.
4. Run any Snappi test that depends on tgen_port_info, for example:
```
pytest tests/snappi_tests/pfc/test_pfc_pause_lossless_with_snappi.py \
    --testbed=<testbed-name> \
    --inventory=<inventory> \
    --host-pattern=<dut> \
    --testbed_file=<testbed.yaml>
```
5. Compare DUT/Snappi ports used in each [tgen_port_info0] / [tgen_port_info1] (or subtype-named) iteration.
6. Optional: remove multidut_port_info for that testbed and rerun. Confirm the test is parametrized only from snappi_port_selection / *links.csv, not from leftover override subtypes.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

### Expected behavior:
- If rdma_ports are present in variables.override.yml, every DUT (single-ASIC, multi-ASIC, single-DUT, multi-DUT) should call get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() so each parametrized iteration uses that subtype’s Tx/Rx subset, intersected with *links.csv.
- Iteration 'long-to-short-400Gbps' and iteration 'short-to-short-100Gbps' must not share the same Tx/Rx set when the override lists different ports.
- If rdma_ports / multidut_port_info is not present, run one combination derived from snappi_ports / snappi_port_selection for what the DUT actually has (e.g. 400.0-single_linecard_single_asic on single-ASIC). Do not emit extra iterations that replay the same ports.

Proposed fix (no patch in this issue):
Drop the if is_snappi_multidut(duthosts): guard in tgen_port_info (the check currently around line 2461 on master; previously cited near 2508 as the file moved) and always call get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() on the override path. Keep the is_override is False branch as the “no rdma_ports” path: snappi_port_selection only, no duplicate runs.

### Actual Behavior:
On single-DUT / single-ASIC (is_snappi_multidut is False):

- Override subtypes are still collected as separate pytest params.
- rdma_ports is only used for “enough Tx/Rx?” skip checks.
- snappi_ports = get_snappi_ports (full *links.csv list) is passed to snappi_dut_base_config() every time.
- Every iteration configures the same ports and repeats the same traffic pattern.
- On multi-DUT / modular chassis the helper runs, so those testbeds already get per-subtype Tx/Rx selection.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Representative of a single-ASIC DUT with two override subtypes. Node IDs differ; the port list does not.

============================= test session starts ==============================
collected 2 items
snappi_tests/pfc/test_pfc_pause_lossless_with_snappi.py::test_pfc_pause_lossless[tgen_port_info0] PASSED
snappi_tests/pfc/test_pfc_pause_lossless_with_snappi.py::test_pfc_pause_lossless[tgen_port_info1] PASSED
# Iteration 0 (override subtype: single-line-long-to-short-400Gbps)
# tgen_port_info: is_override=True, is_snappi_multidut=False
# Skipping get_snappi_ports_for_rdma; using full get_snappi_ports from *links.csv
# snappi_ports peer_port list: ['Ethernet0', 'Ethernet4', 'Ethernet8', 'Ethernet128', ...]
# snappi_dut_base_config: configuring all snappi_ports as Tx/Rx for this run
# Iteration 1 (override subtype: single-line-short-to-short-400Gbps)
# tgen_port_info: is_override=True, is_snappi_multidut=False
# Skipping get_snappi_ports_for_rdma; using full get_snappi_ports from *links.csv
# snappi_ports peer_port list: ['Ethernet0', 'Ethernet4', 'Ethernet8', 'Ethernet128', ...]
# SAME port set as iteration 0 — test body is a duplicate
What the same override should produce after always calling get_snappi_ports_for_rdma():

# Iteration 0: get_snappi_ports_for_rdma(rdma_ports=long-to-short)
#   rx=['Ethernet0'], tx=['Ethernet4']
# Iteration 1: get_snappi_ports_for_rdma(rdma_ports=short-to-short)
#   rx=['Ethernet0'], tx=['Ethernet4']
```

resolution.title: snappi:ensure that exact number of ports are used for single_asic tests
resolution.description:
### Description of PR

tgen_port_info in tests/common/snappi_tests/snappi_fixtures.py selects the Tx/Rx ports every Snappi RDMA test runs on. It has two branches: an override branch driven by multidut_port_info in tests/snappi_tests/variables.override.yml, and a dynamic branch driven by snappi_port_selection built from ansible/files/*links.csv.

This PR fixes following defect in that fixture.

Override port selection was gated on is_snappi_multidut. The override branch only called get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() when is_snappi_multidut(duthosts) was True. On a single-DUT (including single-ASIC) testbed that helper never ran, so rdma_ports was used only for the "are enough ports defined?" skip checks and the full get_snappi_ports list from *links.csv was passed straight into snappi_dut_base_config(). Every parametrized subtype therefore configured the same ports, and the test body was re-run identically for each entry in multidut_port_info. The gate is removed so the helper runs whenever an override exists, regardless of DUT type.

Please note that this pull-request is ONLY changes the tgen_port_info function and nothing else.

Summary:
Fixes #27680

Removed the if is_snappi_multidut(duthosts): guard around get_snappi_ports_for_rdma() so override-driven Tx/Rx selection applies to single-DUT and single-ASIC testbeds, not just modular chassis and multi-DUT.

### Test result

### Approach
#### What is the motivation for this PR?
On single-ASIC and single-DUT testbeds, Snappi RDMA tests were not exercising the port combinations their configuration described. Operators define multiple subtypes in variables.override.yml (for example short-to-long and long-to-short) precisely to cover different traffic paths, but the is_snappi_multidut gate discarded those definitions and reused one port set for every iteration. That burns testbed time on duplicate runs and silently loses the intended coverage, while the same testbeds on modular chassis get correct per-subtype selection.

This was also necessary for single-ASIC DUTs in case they used different speed interfaces using breakout_config and had the definitions in both links.csv and variables.override.yml file.

#### How did you do it?
In tgen_port_info:

Deleted the is_snappi_multidut(duthosts) conditional in the override branch and the now-redundant snappi_ports = get_snappi_ports assignment, calling get_snappi_ports_for_rdma(get_snappi_ports, rdma_ports, tx_port_count, rx_port_count, testbed) unconditionally. The existing pytest_require checks inside that helper still guard against override entries whose hostname/port_name do not match ansible/files/*links.csv.

#### How did you verify/test it?

Ran the test with single-ASIC DUT with two combinations mentioned in the variables.override.yml file and ensured that each combination is executed for each test.
